video_caption: A man's hands are central to the frame, initially holding a red gas canister and rotating it. In the background, to the left, another gas canister with a camping stove attached is visible. A white circular logo in the top-left corner features a bearded man with crossed axes and the text "BUSHCRATY STE STAY CRAFTY". The man puts down the red canister and picks up the camping stove, which is attached to an orange and black gas canister, demonstrating how it works. He then detaches the stove, placing it back in the background, and holds up the orange and black gas canister. He points to the valve at the top and the labels on the side of the canister, which read "COLEMAN", "C100 XTREME 2.0" (repeated), "100g e", "BUTANE/PROPANE MIXTURE" (and "MIESZANKA PROPANU I BUTANU" which is Polish for "PROPANE AND BUTANE MIXTURE"), along with warning symbols for flammability (flame), health hazard (exclamation mark), and environmental hazard (dead tree and fish). He discusses the cost of the canister, stating it was "10 pounds and 50 pence", and mentions it yields "60-70 normal boils". Throughout the segment, his left wrist sports a brown-strapped watch.

A person, wearing a watch with a brown leather strap on their right wrist, holds a red gas canister in their left hand, resting it on a speckled countertop. Their right index finger points to the top of the canister, specifically at the metal valve and the surrounding red surface where the white text "PRIMUS" and a flame hazard symbol are visible. The background reveals a kitchen setting with appliances like a white blender, a dark pot, and a stainless steel sink. The person then slightly moves their right hand, making a small gesture, while still holding the red canister.

In a kitchen setting, a person demonstrates how to transfer gas between canisters, initially showcasing two types of gas canisters, one with a black cap and another light-colored canister labeled "FiveStar" that features a distinctive "bayonet fitting" on its top, which the person points to. The person then presents a small, gold-colored brass valve with a black O-ring and a tiny brass nipple, describing it as a one-way valve essential for the gas transfer. Subsequently, the scene shifts to a "WeightWatchers" digital kitchen scale resting on a speckled countertop, displaying "0000". A red, cylindrical gas canister with printed text including "DOT-SP10677" and "Made in Korea" is placed on the scale, registering a weight of "0383g". The canister is briefly removed, shaken to reveal it's almost empty, and then placed back on the scale, again showing "0383g".

The video opens with a close-up of a speckled countertop, featuring a blurred box for a "WindMaster micro regulator" by "SOTO" in the background. A hand quickly brings a white gas canister into focus, revealing its top with a central valve. A finger then inserts a small brass adapter, which has a black O-ring, into this valve. The adapter is fully seated, showing its gold and black components. The scene then transitions to a red gas canister, also on the speckled countertop, showing its top with a similar valve structure surrounded by a metal ring. The brand "PRIMUS" is prominently displayed on the red canister, along with the text "POWER GAS PROPANE/ISOBUTANE MIX 230 G/8.1OZ - 460 ML e B20" (POWER GAS PROPANE/ISOBUTANE MIX 230 grams/8.1 ounces - 460 milliliters e B20), indicating the type and quantity of gas.

The video opens with a close-up of a red Primus gas canister, clearly labeled "PRIMUS POWER GAS PROPANE/ISOBUTANE MIX 230 G/8.1OZ. 460 ML," resting on a speckled countertop. A hand then brings a smaller, lighter-colored gas canister and connects its nozzle to the valve of the red canister, pressing down to initiate a gas transfer, indicated by a visible puff of mist and a continuous hissing sound. After approximately 25 seconds of gas transferring, the hand lifts the smaller canister away. The scene then transitions to a silver WeightWatchers digital kitchen scale, also on the speckled countertop, displaying "0". The red Primus canister is placed onto the scale, and the display immediately shows "278", indicating its new weight after the gas transfer.

A person's light-skinned hand is shown placing a red gas canister, labeled "PRIMUS" and adorned with hazard symbols for flammability, CO2, and a pictograph of an exploding person, onto a silver Weight Watchers kitchen scale. The scale's digital display initially reads "121G" (121 grams), and it features buttons like "ON/ZERO," "OFF," "INPUT," "RECIPE," "CE," "POINTS," "ENTER," and an alphanumeric keypad, with its maximum capacity indicated as "Max. 3kg (6lb 9.8oz)." The hand then removes the red canister, causing the scale to reset to "0." Following this, the hand reappears, holding a smaller, silver gas canister upside down and aligning its nozzle with the valve on top of the red "PRIMUS" canister, which is now resting on a speckled countertop. Text clearly visible on the red canister includes "UN 2037," "Danger - Gefahr - Danger," "DOT-SP10677," and "Made in Korea." The hand then applies pressure, pushing the silver canister down onto the red one, initiating the process of refilling the red gas canister.

In a close-up shot, a person's hands are shown connecting a light gray gas canister to a red gas canister, which rests on a speckled countertop. The red canister has "PRIMUS" printed in red letters along its side, along with several hazard symbols including a flame, an exclamation mark, and a CO2 symbol. Text visible on the red canister reads: "UN 2037", "Danger - Gefahr - Danger" (Danger), "Feuer - Fire - Feu - Fara - Gevaar" (Fire - Fire - Fire - Danger - Danger), "Perigos - Pericole - Pericol" (Dangers - Dangers - Danger), "Gefahrenzeichen schwer - Gasesty" (Hazard signs heavy - Gas type), "DOT-SP10677", and "Made in Korea". After a moment, the person's hands detach the gray canister from the red one, revealing the valve mechanism on top of the red canister. In the blurred background, part of a black box with the word "Master" visible on it can be seen.

A person, wearing a silver watch on their left wrist, is demonstrating how to refill a small gas canister from a larger red "PRIMUS" canister, which displays hazard symbols (flammable, irritant) and labels "UN 2037" and "DOT-SP10677 Made in Korea" (Made in Korea). Initially, they press a gray cylindrical canister onto the red one, then lift it to reveal a red sticker on its base that reads "Refill" (Refill), indicating it's been previously filled. They then pick up a second, similar silver-colored canister and attempt to connect it to the red canister, stating the importance of ensuring the nipple is properly seated. After an initial lack of sound, the person applies more pressure, and a distinct hissing sound confirms that gas is transferring from the red canister to the smaller one. Once the refilling is complete, the small canister is removed, and the scene transitions to show a "WeightWatchers" brand digital kitchen scale. The red "PRIMUS" canister is then placed on the scale, which displays "288", likely indicating its weight in grams after the refill.

In the video segment, the initial shot focuses on a silver Weight Watchers digital kitchen scale resting on a speckled countertop. A red gas canister with hazard symbols (flame, explosion) is placed on the scale, which displays "303" grams. To the left, a black box with "WindMaster OD-1RXN" text is partially visible. A hand with a light skin tone reaches into the frame, pressing the "KL 5" button on the scale. The display briefly changes before settling back to "303" grams. The hand then lifts the red gas canister off the scale. The scene transitions to a wider shot of the same kitchen countertop, now showing the red gas canister with a small silver camping stove burner attached to its top. A yellow utility lighter lies beside it. In the background, various kitchen appliances are visible, including a white toaster with a box labeled "CRUMPETS" next to it, a white electric kettle, and a silver coffee machine.

The video segment takes place in a kitchen, showing a speckled countertop with various appliances. On the left, a white toaster with wooden accents is visible, along with an orange package of "CRUMPETS" above it. Behind the toaster, a white kettle with a wooden handle is seen, and to the right, a silver coffee machine. In the center, a small, red gas canister with a silver, portable camping stove burner attached to its top sits on the counter. A yellow gas lighter rests beside the stove. A person, wearing an orange short-sleeved shirt over a black long-sleeved shirt and a watch on their left wrist, is interacting with the stove. The person points at the stove (at 0:07 and 0:31), touches the gas canister (at 0:12), and places a black mug on the counter (at 0:17) after picking it up from out of frame. The hands are also seen near the yellow lighter, suggesting an action related to lighting the stove.

The video opens at 0:05 with a close-up of a person's hands on a kitchen countertop, adjusting a small red gas canister with a silver camping stove on top, which is already lit and producing a bright blue flame. The person, wearing a watch on their left wrist, is seen turning a knob on the canister to regulate the flame. In the background, a cream-colored toaster with wooden accents, a white electric kettle, and a silver coffee machine are visible. A package of "CRUMPETS" rests on top of the toaster. At 0:17, the scene cuts to a tight close-up of the camping stove burner, revealing the intricate pattern of bright turquoise-blue flames emanating from numerous small holes arranged in concentric circles on the burner head.

The video opens with a close-up shot of a portable gas stove burner emitting a vibrant turquoise-blue flame, with a small orange-red glow in its center, against a dark, blurry background. The flame flickers subtly until it is extinguished. The scene then transitions to a brightly lit kitchen counter, where a person's hands, wearing a brown-strapped watch, are shown holding two small, cylindrical gas canisters. One canister has a red sticker with the word "refill" (English: refill) written on it, indicating it has been replenished, while both canisters display red labels on their black bases that read "C100 XTREME 2.0". The person places the canisters on a silver kitchen scale and then gestures towards a collection of camping equipment on the counter, including a red Primus stove, various gas canisters, and other stove components, with a white toaster visible in the background. The segment concludes with the person making a fist gesture.
